title_prefix: Every periodic flush empties the whole c
mechanism: Core computes empty_cache = (mode == FORCE_FLUSH) || fCacheLarge || fCacheCritical (refs/bitcoin/src/validation.cpp:2761-2766 at d3056bc) and then chooses `empty_cache ? CoinsTip().Flush() : CoinsTip().Sync()` (:2812). fCacheLarge and fCacheCritical are the two SIZE tiers; fPeriodicWrite -- the DATABASE_WRITE_INTERVAL timer, the analogue of our 600 s / 25 000-block triggers -- is deliberately NOT in empty_cache, so a write driven by the timer alone commits the dirty coins and KEEPS the entries. Our %flush-chainstate Phase 2 calls (bl.store:coins-view-cache-flush view :sync t) unconditionally (src/node/flush.lisp:274); that function stages the dirty coins and then CLRHASHes the entry table and zeroes mem-bytes (src/storage/coins-view-cache.lisp:453-476). The trigger that fired is never passed down: maybe-periodic-flush decides among three conditions (src/node/flush.lisp:369-379) and then calls %flush-chainstate with no argument saying which, and once ANY of them fires it flushes every OTHER chainstate too (:386-389), so a clean chainstate's warm cache is dropped as well. We already have the exact Sync counterpart -- coins-view-cache-sync (src/storage/coins-view-cache.lisp:381-451), written for the RPC walk sites precisely so gettxoutsetinfo would stop throwing away the warm cache -- and the flush path simply never chooses it.
consequence: Correctness is unaffected: a cleared cache is refilled by pull-through reads, and my probe confirms every entry is found again. The cost is the re-warm. Measured on a LevelDB-backed cache with 200,000 coins: a full read pass costs 0.005 s while the entries are cached and 0.141 s on the first pass after coins-view-cache-flush, i.e. about 680 ns of extra pull-through per entry, a 28x pass cost; after coins-view-cache-sync the same pass stays at 0.005 s. Per-entry memory accounting is 225 bytes, so the default 450 MiB budget (*coins-cache-budget-bytes* = 471,859,200) holds about 2.05M entries at the LARGE threshold -- a time-triggered flush can therefore discard ~2.05M warm entries that Core would have kept, at a floor of ~1.4 s of pull-through to re-read them, and that floor is measured against a LevelDB whose data was just written and is still in its own cache; on a mainnet chainstate the misses are real disk reads and cost far more. Traced but not measured end to end: at the tip the 600 s timer elapses between most blocks (blocks arrive ~1 per 10 minutes and maybe-periodic-flush runs on every :updated-block-tip, src/node/flush.lisp:346), so a following node empties its coins cache at nearly every connect and -dbcache buys it almost nothing after IBD. I did not run an IBD to show a wall-clock sync regression, so I am not claiming the S2 'measurable sync slowdown reaching an operator' -- S3, bounded divergence with a quantified per-flush cost.
evidence: Container /Users/sen/common-lisp/bl-ga11v-misc-s3b, warm image. (a) build/ga11probe/flushmeas2.lisp, 200,000 coins over a real coins-view-db: ((:FIRST-PULL-PASS (0.134)) (:ENTRIES 200000) (:WARM-HIT-PASSES (0.005 0.005 0.005)) (:ENTRIES-AFTER-SYNC 200000) (:PASSES-AFTER-SYNC (0.005 0.005 0.005)) (:ENTRIES-AFTER-FLUSH 0) (:FIRST-PASS-AFTER-FLUSH (0.141)) (:SUBSEQUENT-PASSES-AFTER-FLUSH (0.011 0.011))). Sync keeps 200,000 entries and the pass cost; Flush drops to 0 entries and the next pass costs 28x. (b) Sizing: 200,000 entries report cvc-mem-bytes 45,000,000 = 225 bytes/entry; large-coins-cache-threshold of the 471,859,200-byte default budget divides to 2,050,548 entries. (c) build/ga11probe/flushcs.lisp drives the REAL periodic path on a real chainstate (init-chain-state + open-chainstate-coins-view, 50,000 coins) and calls bl::%flush-chainstate exactly as the trigger does: (:ENTRIES-BEFORE 50000 :MEM-BEFORE 11250000 :ENTRIES-AFTER-OUR-PERIODIC-FLUSH 0 :MEM-AFTER 0 :ENTRIES-AFTER-REWARM 50000 :ENTRIES-AFTER-CORE-STYLE-SYNC 50000). Ours: src/node/flush.lisp:23-31, :274, :346-358, :369-392; src/storage/coins-view-cache.lisp:381-451 (sync), :453-476 (flush). Core: validation.cpp:2761-2766, :2812.
fix_shape: Pass the trigger down and let it choose the branch, exactly as Core does. maybe-periodic-flush already knows which of the three conditions fired; have it compute Core's empty_cache -- true only for the size trigger (our large-coins-cache-threshold, Core's fCacheLarge) and for the CRITICAL/forced cases (maybe-critical-flush, shutdown, reindex) -- and hand it to %flush-chainstate as a keyword, which Phase 2 turns into coins-view-cache-sync when false and coins-view-cache-flush when true. Note the caller contract already written on coins-view-cache-sync's docstring: the node lock must be held across the call and the batch creation, which the flush path already satisfies. The fan-out to the other chainstates (src/node/flush.lisp:386-389) must inherit the same choice, so a clean chainstate flushed only because a sibling triggered takes the Sync branch. Keep the shutdown, reindex and disk-space-abort paths on Flush, since Core's FORCE_FLUSH is in empty_cache. A regression test should assert that a time/count-triggered flush leaves the cache entry count unchanged while a size-triggered one empties it, with both directions asserted so the test cannot pass vacuously.
